name: Umqombothi
description: Sorghum and maize beer, thick and porridge-like, brewed at home for ceremonies. Drunk from a shared clay pot passed clockwise.
funFact: Umqombothi is central to Xhosa and Zulu ceremony — brewing it is how ancestors are honoured at weddings and funerals, so the beer is a ritual object as much as a drink.

serve.how: Serve at room temperature from a communal clay pot, never chilled and never individually glassed. Stir before serving, since the solids settle fast and the texture is part of it — this is a beer you can almost eat. Protocol matters: the pot is passed in one direction and the brewer or elder drinks first.

composition.summary: A thick, sour sorghum-and-maize beer fermented with wild lactic cultures.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Sorghum malt with unmalted maize meal.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild yeast alongside lactic bacteria, giving a yoghurt-like sourness.

components.label: Other
components.detail: The beer is served unfiltered, with the grain solids still suspended.

composition.process: Maize meal and sorghum malt are cooked, soured overnight, boiled and then fermented for a day or two before being drunk immediately, still actively fermenting.

name: Tella
description: Ethiopia's home-brewed beer, made with gesho instead of hops and often flavoured by the smoked gourd it ferments in. Smoky, sour and served in a flask.
funFact: Gesho — the same buckthorn that bitters tej honey wine — stands in for hops, and the fermenting vessel is often smoked with olive wood, which is where the beer's signature smokiness comes from.

serve.how: Serve cool or at ambient temperature in a flask or plain glass, cloudy and unfiltered. Expect smoke on the nose before anything else, then a dry, grainy sourness. It is a house beer rather than a bar beer, so treat variation between batches as the point rather than a fault.

composition.summary: A smoky, gesho-bittered grain beer fermented in a smoke-cured vessel.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Barley, often with teff, sorghum or maize.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None — gesho, a native buckthorn, provides the bitterness.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild fermentation from the vessel and the environment.

components.label: Other
components.detail: The clay or gourd vessel, cured with olive-wood smoke.

composition.process: Roasted grain and gesho are fermented together in a smoke-cured vessel for several days to a week, then served unfiltered.

name: Bouza
description: A thick, living grain beer with a claim to being among the oldest continuously made brews on earth — closer to the beer of the pharaohs than anything with hops in it.
funFact: Bouza is made by fermenting partly baked bread loaves, a method archaeologists recognise from ancient Egyptian brewing scenes — the bread is the mash, not an ingredient added to it.

serve.how: Serve at ambient temperature in a plain vessel — it is thick, opaque and still actively fermenting, so a sealed bottle is a bad idea. Stir before pouring since it separates fast. Expect something between beer and liquid bread, sour and yeasty rather than crisp.

composition.summary: A live, unfiltered wheat beer fermented from partially baked bread loaves.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Coarsely ground wheat, part of it malted, part baked into loaves.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild and carried-over yeast, left active in the finished beer.

components.label: Other
components.detail: The bread loaves themselves, which supply both starch and fermentation.

composition.process: Loaves of lightly baked wheat bread are crumbled into water with malted wheat and fermented for a day or two, then drunk while still cloudy and active.

name: Chibuku
description: Opaque sorghum beer sold in a waxed carton you shake before opening. Still fermenting on the shelf, sour and porridge-thick — 'shake shake' is its actual nickname.
funFact: The carton is deliberately unsealed so the still-active fermentation can vent — a sealed container would burst, which is why Chibuku is one of the few commercial beers that cannot be bottled.

serve.how: Shake the carton hard before opening to resuspend the solids, then drink straight from it — that is the intended vessel and pouring into a glass gains nothing. Expect it thick, sour and actively fizzing. Its shelf life is measured in days, and it keeps getting sourer and stronger the whole time.

composition.summary: A commercially produced opaque sorghum beer sold while still actively fermenting.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Sorghum malt with maize meal.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild and pitched yeast alongside lactic bacteria.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Sold unfiltered and unpasteurised, still fermenting in the carton.

composition.process: Maize and sorghum are soured, cooked and briefly fermented, then packaged live and distributed within days.

name: Dolo
description: West African sorghum beer brewed and sold by women in open-air cabarets, ladled warm from a clay pot and drunk the day it is ready.
funFact: Dolo brewing is almost exclusively women's work across Burkina Faso and Mali, and the cabarets where it is sold function as the village's social and economic centre as much as a bar.

serve.how: Serve warm or at ambient temperature in a calabash, ladled from the communal pot. It is cloudy and lightly sour, with smoke from the wood-fired brewing. Drink it the day it is made — by the second day it has soured well past pleasant, which is why brewing happens on a fixed weekly rhythm.

composition.summary: A wild-fermented sorghum beer brewed over wood fire and sold the same day.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Germinated and sun-dried sorghum.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild yeast, often carried over in the unwashed brewing pot.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Wood smoke from the open fire used to boil the wort.

composition.process: Sorghum is germinated, dried, milled and boiled over wood fire, then fermented overnight with wild organisms and sold immediately.

name: Mbege
description: Chagga banana beer from the slopes of Kilimanjaro: ripe bananas fermented with malted finger millet, thick, sour and central to every ceremony.
funFact: Among the Chagga, mbege is required at weddings, funerals and dispute settlements — it functions as a social contract as much as a drink, and brewing takes several days of coordinated work.

serve.how: Serve at ambient temperature from a shared vessel, stirred first since it separates. Expect a thick, cloudy, distinctly sour drink with strong banana character and grit from the millet. It is drunk in company and in quantity; a small tasting pour misses the point of a beer built for ceremony.

composition.summary: A banana beer fermented with malted finger millet as the saccharifying agent.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: Malted finger millet, which converts the banana sugars.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild yeast and lactic bacteria from the fruit and the vessel.

components.label: Other
components.detail: Ripe bananas, boiled down over days as the fermentable base.

composition.process: Bananas are ripened, boiled and combined with malted millet flour, then fermented in covered gourds for two to four days.

name: Muratina
description: Kikuyu honey beer fermented with the dried fruit of the sausage tree, which carries the yeast. Sweet, sour and reserved for elders and ceremony.
funFact: The muratina fruit is not an ingredient for flavour but a yeast vector — dried and soaked pieces carry the fermenting culture, and a good piece is reused across many brews.

serve.how: Serve at ambient temperature in a gourd or horn, poured from the communal container. It is honey-sweet at the front and sour behind, with a faint woody tannin from the fruit. Traditionally it was restricted to elders and ceremonial occasions rather than drunk casually, and it is still treated with some of that formality.

composition.summary: A honey and sugarcane ferment inoculated by dried sausage-tree fruit.

components.label: Malt
components.detail: None — honey and sugarcane juice provide the fermentables.

components.label: Hops
components.detail: None.

components.label: Yeast
components.detail: Wild yeast carried on dried muratina (sausage tree) fruit.

components.label: Other
components.detail: The muratina fruit itself, reused between batches as a starter.

composition.process: Honey and cane juice are diluted and inoculated with soaked muratina fruit, then fermented for two to four days before being served.
